ov: A huge Arctic pinniped with long ivory tusks, bristly whiskers and a nearly hairless body. It spends much of its life on the sea ice, feeding on clams and other shellfish from the sea floor.

why.et: Indigenous Arctic peoples have long hunted walruses for meat, fat, skin, tusks and bone.

wt: 600–1,500 kg; Pacific males can top 2,000 kg
rg: Shallow Arctic seas over the continental shelves.
df: Mainly bivalve molluscs such as clams, found on the sea floor.

cf.tip: A walrus is bigger than any seal except the elephant seals, and has long tusks and almost hairless skin.

fx: Walruses have fatally injured polar bears with their tusks.
